recentItems.title: China warns of consequences following France's penalties targeting Shein and Temu
recentItems.description:
(3 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beijing, China - 3 September 2026
1. Wide of spokesperson of Chinese commerce ministry, Huang Ling addressing the media
2. Wide of journalist asking question
3. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Huang Ling, spokesperson of Chinese Commerce Ministry: 
“China expresses strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to France insisting on implementing this clearly discriminatory trade restriction.”
4. Wide of journalists at the news briefing
5. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Huang Ling, spokesperson of Chinese Commerce Ministry:
“Under the guise of enacting the so-called “environmental protection” and “sustainable” standards, the law in fact imposed exclusionary measures. It is suspected of violating the WTO principle of non-discrimination and constituted a trade barrier against China. It is severely against the principles of fair competition and free trade promoted by France, which will not only harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies but also hurt the interests of French consumers.”
6. Wide of journalists 
7. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Huang Ling, spokesperson of Chinese Commerce Ministry: 
“If France insists on going its own way, China will take necessary measures to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies. The French side will bear full responsibility for any consequences that result.”
8. Various of news conference
STORYLINE:
China on Thursday warned of potential consequences over a newly enacted French law that imposes penalties on ultra-fast-fashion retailers, including Shein and Temu.

France has enacted an anti-fast-fashion law that imposes penalties on clothing, footwear and household linen products sold by companies classified as “ultra-fast fashion” retailers, including Chinese e-commerce platforms Shein and Temu.

Chinese Commerce Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling criticized the measures as “discriminatory,” saying the law imposes exclusionary measures under the guise of setting environmental production and sustainability standards.

“It is severely against the principles of fair competition and free trade promoted by France, which will not only harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies but also hurt the interests of French consumers,” Huang said.

Huang said China strongly opposed the trade restrictions and warned that Beijing could take countermeasures if France proceeded with them.

“If France insists on going its own way, China will take necessary measures to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies,” Huang said. “The French side will bear full responsibility for any consequences that result.”

AP Video shot by Borg Wong

recentItems.title: John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell and 'Wild Horse Nine' cast arrive in Venice
recentItems.description:
(3 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Venice - 3 September 2026
1. Sam Rockwell on the back of boat with Ailín Salas
2. John Malkovich waving from dock
3. Steve Buscemi waving to photographers
4. Various of cast and crew assembling for photos
5. Various of photocall of (R-L) Graham Broadbent, John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Parker Posey, Ailín Salas, Mariana di Girolamo, Steve Buscemi, director Martin McDonagh and Anita Overland 
5. Various of photocall of (R-L) John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Parker Posey, Ailín Salas, Mariana di Girolamo, Steve Buscemi, and director Martin McDonagh 
5. Various of photocall of Sam Rockwell, Martin McDonagh and John Malkovich
6. Various of Steve Buscemi and Parker Posey posing
7. Various of Buscemi signing autographs
STORYLINE:
The stars of "Wild Horse Nine" docked in Venice Thursday ahead of the film's press conference.

"Wild Horse Nine,"which was written and directed by Martin McDonagh, is one of the higher-profile films launching at the 83rd edition of the festival. The film stars Sam Rockwell and John Malkovich as CIA agents who are dispatched to Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup. It will have a theatrical release later this fall, and, if McDonagh’s track record is any indication, might be an awards player.

McDonagh’s previous two films, “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” and “The Banshees of Inisherin” both bowed at Venice and went on to receive multiple Oscar nominations, including best picture. “Three Billboards” won two, for Rockwell and Frances McDormand.

recentItems.title: Fighting in southwestern Somalia between government forces and local militia injures dozens
recentItems.description:
(3 Sep 2026) 
Clients note: This item contains on-screen graphics, including AP branding.

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS  
Baidoa, Somalia - 3 September 2026
1. Wide of residents watching as soldiers walk, heavily armed
2. Mid shot of blood on the road ++GRAPHIC++
3. Wide of residents watching as armed soldiers ride past in a pick up 
4. Various of damaged home
5. Mid of residents looking at blood soldier uniform ++GRAPHIC++
6. Ambulance racing past residents
7. Soldiers racing past residents in pick ups
STORYLINE:
Fighting erupted early Thursday between Somali government forces and militia aligned with former South West state President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen on the outskirts of Baidoa, with heavy gunfire reported and civilians fleeing some neighborhoods.

The fighting began around 5 a.m. local time, according to residents. 

Somalia’s Defence Ministry said government forces were responding to an attack on their positions by militia aligned with Laftagareen and al-Shabab fighters.

Abdullahi Haji, a Baidoa resident, told AP on the phone that he left his home after the fighting began, fearing the clashes could spread into his neighborhood. 

He said he heard heavy gunfire and that stray bullets had landed in residential areas.

Dr. Abdikafi Omar Mohamud, head of the emergency department at Bay Regional Hospital, told the Associated Press that his hospital had received 24 people wounded in the fighting and one civilian who died.

The clashes are the latest escalation in a political and security dispute between Somalia’s federal government and Laftagareen’s camp over control of South West state. 

Federal forces took control of Baidoa on March 30, after which Laftagareen resigned. He had governed the state since 2018.

The latest major fighting in and around Baidoa occurred on August 17, when government forces and Laftagareen-aligned fighters clashed.

Baidoa, about 245 kilometers (150 miles) northwest of Mogadishu, is a major humanitarian hub and hosts large numbers of people displaced by conflict and drought.

The situation remained fluid Thursday, with no independently verified information on the overall casualties or extent of the fighting.

AP Video by Bishar Mukhtar
